messages:
maya: Quick q — can the gateway resolve ambiguous selectors deterministically without exploding the rule count? seeing odd canary fallbacks this morning :thinking_face:
prashant: What does "ambiguous" look like here? host+path collisions? header anchors? a short example would help
maya: sure, simplified: ```json
[
  {"id":"r1","host":"api.example.com","path":"/users/*","service":"svc-a"},
  {"id":"r2","host":"*.example.com","path":"/users/123","service":"svc-b"},
  {"id":"r3","host":"api.example.com","headers":{"X-Region":"eu"},"service":"svc-canary"}
]
```
maya: when a request hits api.example.com/users/123 with X-Region absent, it sometimes picks r1 and sometimes r2 depending on deploy order — we need deterministic tie-breaks
emily: we should avoid implicit randomness. two ideas: (1) explicit `priority` on rules that users can set, (2) deterministic scoring function (specificity weight + explicit priority + stable fallback like rule UUID). for UX (2) requires an explain panel so users can see why score was chosen :eyes:
josh: +1 for show-why. if we hide scoring heuristics users will be confused. console should show contributing factors and final score, e.g. `hostScore=6,pathScore=8,headerScore=0,priority=0 -> total=14`
prashant: agreed. implement scoring but keep a stable tie-breaker: sort by `priority` desc, then `specificity` desc, then `created_at` asc (or rule UUID) so two equally-scored rules don't flip when we recompile
maya: can we also support an optional `resolver_hint` field that only affects tie-break ordering (not primary matching)? e.g. `resolver_hint: "prefer-service-chunk"` so customers can nudge without adding full priority management
emily: `resolver_hint` sounds useful for migrations/canaries. default behaviour should still be deterministic if hint absent. also route telemetry should include `resolution_trace_id` and for debug mode output the score breakdown to logs
routebot: routebot: matched rule=r1 fallback_used=false score=14 compiled=9ms trace_id=rt-2055-9a3b
josh: also think about header-derived anchors: treat certain headers (X-Service, X-Canary) as anchors with very high weight so they win over broad host globs. but make anchors opt-in in config to avoid surprising behavior
maya: rollout impact: if fallback goes to a service with different quota buckets we should expose that in the canary UI (show expected quota consumption + latency delta). otherwise teams get weird billing spikes
prashant: good point — console should show "effective route" for a sample request (what service, what quota bucket). that's part of the explain panel
emily: tests: add fuzz tests that generate colliding selectors and assert deterministic selection across many compiles. also add integration test where header anchor toggles selection
josh: UX stub: Console -> Route -> Explain -> shows: matched_rule, match_score_breakdown, fallback_chain, effective_service, quota_bucket, trace_link. and a "why-not" list for near-misses
maya: I'll draft RFC for: scoring formula, `resolver_hint`, stable tie-break order (priority -> specificity -> created_at/uuid), telemetry fields (resolution_trace_id + score_breakdown), and console explain panel. tagging for review @prashant @emily :+1:
prashant: happy to review, will carve out time tomorrow :+1:
emily: I'll sketch the UI mock and sample payload for the trace endpoint :sparkles:
routebot: routebot: scheduled job: recompile-route-index at 2055552000, will emit traces for debug-enabled namespaces
maya: thanks folks — this should stop the flakiness we saw in canary routing
